title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: analytic moduli of elliptic curves equipped with an oriented ('strict' or 'divergente') Torelli structure, meaning an ordered basis (z1,z2) of the period lattice H_s inside the tangent line t_E. The invariant τ = z2/z1 lies in the upper half-plane D+. D+ is the fine moduli space, with universal family X_{D+} = (D+ × C)/Z^2.

This page: SL(2,Z) acts on the right on the set of isomorphism classes of such structures by t ↦ t∘g, i.e. by change of basis. Writing the basis as a row vector and multiplying by g = (a b; c d) gives z1' = a z1 + c z2 and z2' = b z1 + d z2. The invariant then transforms as τ' = z2'/z1' = (dτ + b)/(cτ + a), which is formula (10). This is a right action of SL(2,Z) on D+. Grothendieck then begins converting it to a left action via t ↦ t∘g^{-1}.

On the next page he lifts the action to the universal family: the isomorphism E_τ → E_{τ∘g} is multiplication by 1/(a + cτ). After composing with the involution (a b; c d) ↦ (d b; c a) applied to g^{-1}, he recovers the standard left action g·(τ, z) = ((aτ + b)/(cτ + d), z/(cτ + d)) on (D+ × C)/Z^2.

Purpose: to make explicit the SL(2,Z) symmetry of the analytic modular situation, so that the modular stack of elliptic curves can be presented as the quotient [X_{D+}/SL(2,Z)] → [D+/SL(2,Z)]. This prepares the comparison with the algebraic moduli in characteristic ≠ 2 (Legendre/level-2 structures) treated in this dossier.
errors: No mathematical error. Since det g = 1, cτ + a ≠ 0 and Im τ' = Im τ/|cτ + a|^2 > 0, so τ' stays in D+. With the basis written as a row vector multiplied on the right by g, t ↦ t∘g is indeed a right action.

The convention is nonstandard: it yields (dτ + b)/(cτ + a) rather than (aτ + b)/(cτ + d). Grothendieck corrects for this on the next page with an extra involution swapping a and d. This is merely awkward bookkeeping, not an error.

ideas.what: Right action of SL(2,Z) on oriented period bases (Torelli structures) and the induced Möbius action on τ, formula (10)
ideas.modern_name: Modular group action on the upper half-plane via change of oriented lattice basis
ideas.where_published: Standard textbook material (e.g. Serre, Cours d'arithmétique; Deligne–Rapoport). No specific Grothendieck publication known.

ideas.what: Presenting the analytic modular situation (D+, X_{D+}) as equipped with an SL(2,Z) action, preparing the quotient description of the moduli stack
ideas.modern_name: Analytic moduli stack M_{1,1}^an = [D+/SL(2,Z)] with universal curve [(D+×C)/(Z^2 ⋊ SL(2,Z))]
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical; stack formulation by Deligne–Mumford/Deligne–Rapoport (1969–1973), later Hain and others
ideas.where_published: The modular tower and fundamental group of M_{1,1} appear in Esquisse d'un programme (1984), but not this explicit computation.

deep.surprise_reason: This is purely classical, didactic material: the SL(2,Z) action on period bases and on τ, written in a slightly unusual right-action convention. Nothing here is absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: Line 2: 'structures de Torelli divisées' should almost certainly read 'structures de Torelli divergentes', matching the term 'divergente' (= stricte) introduced on the previous page.
In (10), the denominator 'cτ + a' has the c written over another letter in the manuscript. It is c, consistent with z1' = a z1 + c z2.
'opère à droite, par t ↦ t∘g' is correct. The manuscript writes 'D+' with a script D and 'X_{D+}' with a script X, and the transcription renders these inconsistently (\mathcal vs \mathfrak).
